Hi, I'm Priya Anand, founder and CEO of FleetPulse. We sell predictive
maintenance software to regional trucking fleets.

**The problem.** Regional trucking fleets — companies running 20 to
200 trucks, not the giant national carriers — lose an average of
several days of revenue per truck every year to unplanned breakdowns.
A single roadside engine failure can cost a small fleet operator
thousands of dollars in towing, emergency repair, missed delivery
penalties, and a driver sitting idle. Most of these fleets still
schedule maintenance on a fixed mileage or calendar interval, not on
the actual condition of the vehicle, because the tools that do
condition-based maintenance were built for huge national fleets with
dedicated data teams.

**Target customer.** Regional and mid-size trucking and logistics
companies, typically family-owned or private-equity-backed, running
20-200 trucks, without an in-house data science or fleet-analytics
team.

**Our solution.** FleetPulse plugs into a truck's existing onboard
diagnostics port with a small hardware sensor we ship to customers,
streams engine, brake, and transmission telemetry to our cloud
platform, and uses a machine-learning model to flag which vehicles are
actually at elevated risk of failure in the next 2-4 weeks — not just
"this truck is due for service" on a fixed schedule. Fleet managers
get a daily dashboard and SMS/email alerts telling them which trucks
to prioritize for inspection.

**Product.** The core product is a web dashboard plus a small physical
sensor (we source the sensor hardware from a third-party manufacturer
and assemble/configure it ourselves before shipping). We charge a
monthly per-truck subscription that includes the sensor, the
dashboard, and alerting.

**Business model.** Straightforward B2B SaaS, billed monthly per
truck under contract, priced at $45/truck/month with a minimum
12-month commitment. No usage-based pricing today.

**Market.** We believe predictive maintenance for regional trucking
fleets is a $40 billion market opportunity. There are roughly 1.2
million trucks operated by fleets in our target size range in the
United States alone.

**Competition.** The main competitor we run into in sales
conversations is FleetIQ, which has raised over $120 million from a
major logistics conglomerate and offers a broader (and more
expensive) fleet-management suite that includes predictive
maintenance as one module among many. There are also a handful of
smaller regional players we don't know much about. Our differentiation
is that we are purpose-built for predictive maintenance specifically,
priced for smaller fleets, and can be installed in under 30 minutes
per truck without an IT team.

**Traction.** We've been selling for about a year. We currently have 4
paying customers under contract, covering 260 trucks combined, for
$420,000 in current annual recurring revenue. One of those four
customers, a regional produce distributor, accounts for 55% of that
revenue. All four customers have renewed at least once. We started the
year at roughly $60,000 in ARR and have grown at approximately 15%
month-over-month for the last six months.

**Customer evidence.** Our largest customer told us that in the six
months after installing FleetPulse, their unplanned roadside
breakdowns dropped by about a third, though we have not yet done a
rigorous before/after study across our full customer base — that's
anecdotal from one customer's fleet manager, not something we've
independently measured across all four accounts.

**Financial history.** Current ARR is $420,000. Our annual cost of
hosting the platform, cellular data for the sensors, and customer
support is approximately $180,000, which gives us gross margins of
around 75%. We are not yet profitable — our total annual operating
costs, including the team and sales, are approximately $890,000, so we
are running a net loss and burning cash.

**Projections.** We are projecting we can reach $1.2 million in ARR
within 12 months if we can close 3-4 more fleets of similar size to
our current customers and continue renewing existing accounts.

**Costs.** Roughly $180,000/year in hosting, data, and support
(cost of revenue); the remainder of our ~$890,000 in annual operating
costs is salaries (five full-time employees including Priya), sensor
hardware inventory, and a small amount of paid marketing.

**Funding request.** We are raising $750,000 for 8% equity.

**Valuation.** We believe this values FleetPulse at roughly $9.375
million post-money.

**Use of funds.** Approximately 60% engineering (two additional
engineers to improve the failure-prediction model and build
integrations with common fleet-management software), 25% sales (one
additional account executive plus travel/trade shows), and 15%
working capital and sensor hardware inventory to support new
customers.

**Team.** I'm Priya Anand, founder and CEO — before FleetPulse I spent
four years in operations at a regional trucking company, which is
where I saw this problem firsthand. Our CTO, Marcus Webb, previously
worked in enterprise software and leads our engineering team of three.
We have a part-time advisor with a background in fleet logistics who
helps with customer introductions.

**Risks.** Our biggest risks are customer concentration (one account
is more than half our revenue), the capital and time required to
acquire new mid-size fleet customers one at a time through direct
sales, and the fact that FleetIQ or another well-funded competitor
could decide to build a cheaper, faster-to-install product aimed at
smaller fleets and use their existing sales relationships to
out-compete us.

**Growth strategy.** We plan to grow primarily through direct outbound
sales to regional fleet operators, referrals from existing customers,
and attending two or three industry trade shows a year. We are also
exploring a possible partnership with a regional truck maintenance
chain to refer customers to us, though that partnership is not yet
signed.

**Timing / why now.** Telematics hardware has gotten cheap enough in
the last few years that a small company like ours can afford to ship
a physical sensor to a customer and still make good gross margins,
which wasn't really economical five years ago. At the same time,
diesel and driver costs have gone up enough that fleet operators are
much more willing to pay for something that reduces unplanned
downtime than they were before.

That's FleetPulse. We're asking for $750,000 for 8% equity to help us
get from $420,000 to $1.2 million in ARR over the next year. Happy to
answer any questions the panel has.
